nahhas-irab:47-47.t: Among the most excellent things reported about it is what Manṣūr reported from Mujāhid, who said: they did deeds which they imagined to be good deeds, and lo, they were evil deeds. And it is said: they did evil deeds and imagined that they would repent before death, but death overtook them; they had thought that they would be saved by repentance, and there appeared to them from Allah what they had not been reckoning on. It is also possible that they imagined that they would be forgiven without repentance, and there appeared to them what they had not been reckoning on, namely entering the Fire.

nahhas-irab:48-48.t: وَبَدا لَهُمْ سَيِّئاتُ: that is, the punishment of the evil deeds, or the mention of the evil deeds.

nahhas-irab:49-49.t: قالَ إِنَّما أُوتِيتُهُ عَلى عِلْمٍ: Abū Isḥāq said: that is, on account of nobility and merit through which this that I have been given is due to me, for I knew that I would be given this. بَلْ هِيَ فِتْنَةٌ: al-Farrāʾ said: it is made feminine because of the feminine gender of «الفتنة» (the trial); and had it been «بل هو فتنة» it would have been permissible. Abū Jaʿfar said: the implied meaning is: rather, I gave it to him as a trial. وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ: that is, they do not know that their being given wealth is a test; and it is said: their conduct is the conduct of one who does not know.

nahhas-irab:50-52.t: قَدْ قالَهَا الَّذِينَ: the feminine pronoun is on the basis that it refers to «الكلمة» (the statement), which is feminine.

nahhas-irab:53-53.t:
قُلْ يا عِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ: if you wish, you may omit the yāʾ, because the vocative (nidāʾ) is a place of omission. Among the most excellent things reported about it is what Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq reported from Nāfiʿ from Ibn ʿUmar, who said:
When we agreed upon the emigration (hijra), I, Hishām ibn al-ʿĀṣī ibn Wāʾil al-Sahmī and ʿAyyāsh ibn ʿUtba made an appointment, and we said: "The meeting place is Aḍāt Ghifār"; and we said: "Whoever of us stays behind has been detained." In the morning I and ʿAyyāsh ibn ʿUtba were there, but Hishām did not come, and it turned out that he had been put to trial and had succumbed to it. In Medina we used to say: "These are people who came to know Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and believed in Him and in His Messenger ﷺ, then they were seduced away by an affliction that befell them; we do not see any repentance for them," and they too used to say this. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed قُلْ يا عِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ لا تَقْنَطُوا مِنْ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ — to the end of the story. And ʿAbd al-Aʿlā reported from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: there were some of the polytheists who had killed and killed much, and committed fornication and done so much; and they said to the Prophet ﷺ — or sent to him —: "What you call us to is surely good, if only you would tell us that there is repentance for us." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: قُلْ يا عِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ — to the end of the verses. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said: this is the most hope-giving verse in the Qurʾān; but Ibn ʿAbbās replied to him, saying:
Rather, the most hope-giving verse in the Qurʾān is وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو مَغْفِرَةٍ لِلنَّاسِ عَلى ظُلْمِهِمْ [al-Raʿd: 6]. And Ḥammād ibn Salama reported from Thābit from Shahr ibn Ḥawshab from Asmāʾ that she heard the Prophet ﷺ recite:
قُلْ يا عِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ لا تَقْنَطُوا مِنْ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعاً «ولا يبالي» ("and He does not care") إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ. And in the codex (muṣḥaf) of Ibn Masʿūd: «إنّ الله يغفر الذّنوب جميعا لمن يشاء» ("Allah forgives all sins, for whom He wills"). These two readings are by way of explanation (tafsīr), that is, He forgives whom He wills; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made known whom He wills to forgive: it is the one who repents, or the one who committed a minor sin and had no major sin. What comes after it indicates that He means the one who repents.

nahhas-irab:54-55.t: وَأَنِيبُوا إِلى رَبِّكُمْ: so the one who repents has all his sins forgiven. That is indicated by وَإِنِّي لَغَفَّارٌ لِمَنْ تابَ [Ṭā Hā: 82]. So this is [the answer to] the difficulty in it. وَأَنِيبُوا إِلى رَبِّكُمْ وَأَسْلِمُوا لَهُ: al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: that is, «أنيبوا» means: return to obedience to Him, Mighty and Majestic, and to His command. Abū Jaʿfar said: then He threatened whoever does not return, saying: مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَكُمُ الْعَذابُ ثُمَّ لا تُنْصَرُونَ, that is, then no one will ward it off from you.

nahhas-irab:56-56.t: أَنْ تَقُولَ نَفْسٌ is in the position of the accusative (naṣb), that is, "out of aversion that a soul should say"; and according to the Kufans it has the meaning of «لئلا تقول نفس» ("lest a soul say"). يا حَسْرَتى: the original is «يا حسرتي», that is, "O my regret!"; the yāʾ was replaced by an alif because it is lighter. The point of addressing regret in the vocative (nidāʾ) is that it carries the meaning that it is inseparable and present, so this is more eloquent than a plain statement. Al-Farrāʾ permitted, in continuous speech (waṣl): «يا حسرتاه على كذا» and «ويا حسرتاه على كذا», and he mentioned this view regarding the verse and likened it to lamentation (nudba). Keeping the hāʾ in continuous speech is an error according to all the grammarians other than him; this is not a place of lamentation, there is no hāʾ in the written text (al-sawād), and no one has read it so. عَلى ما فَرَّطْتُ فِي جَنْبِ اللَّهِ: al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: that is, in the remembrance of Allah; he said: meaning the Qurʾān and acting upon it. And in the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿAjlān from Saʿīd al-Maqburī from Abū Hurayra from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: «No man sits in a sitting, or walks a walk, or lies down in a place of lying down, in which he does not remember Allah, Mighty and Majestic, but that it will be a «ترة» against him on the Day of Resurrection» — that is, a regret. Ibrāhīm al-Taymī said: among the regrets on the Day of Resurrection is that a man sees his wealth, which Allah gave him, on the Day of Resurrection in the balance of someone else who inherited it and used it rightly, so that its reward is his and its burden is upon the other. And among the regrets is that a man sees his slave, whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, entrusted to him in this world, nearer in rank to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, [than himself]; or sees a man he knew who was blind in this world, now seeing on the Day of Resurrection, while he himself has become blind. وَإِنْ كُنْتُ لَمِنَ السَّاخِرِينَ: Abū Isḥāq said: that is, I was nothing but one of the mockers.

nahhas-irab:57-57.t: It is said: its meaning is: if He had guided me to escape from the Fire and returned me to [the state of] legal responsibility (taklīf), لَكُنْتُ مِنَ الْمُتَّقِينَ — [guarding against] acts of disobedience. And it is said: if only Allah had guided me in the world; and he is answered and it is said: بَلى قَدْ جاءَتْكَ آياتِي, that is, I did guide you with clear proofs.

nahhas-irab:58-58.t:
أَوْ تَقُولَ حِينَ تَرَى الْعَذابَ لَوْ أَنَّ لِي كَرَّةً فَأَكُونَ: [فَأَكُونَ] is accusative as the answer to the wish (tamannī); or, if you wish, it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «كرة», because its meaning is «أن أكون» ("that I be"), as [the poet] said: [al-Wāfir] 391-
للبس عباءة وتقرّ عيني ... أحبّ إليّ من لبس الشّفوف
("Wearing a coarse cloak, with my eye content, is dearer to me than wearing sheer fine garments.")

nahhas-irab:59-59.t: بَلى قَدْ جاءَتْكَ آياتِي: with fatḥa on the kāf; and «النفس» (the soul) is feminine, [but the masculine is used] because the meaning refers to a male. ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read it with kasra, treating «النفس» as feminine, and the reading with kasra is reported from the Prophet ﷺ.

nahhas-irab:60-60.t: وَيَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ تَرَى الَّذِينَ كَذَبُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ وُجُوهُهُمْ مُسْوَدَّةٌ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), in the position of the accusative; and the accusative is permissible, on the basis that «وجوههم» is a badal (substitute) for «الذين». أَلَيْسَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ مَثْوىً لِلْمُتَكَبِّرِينَ: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ explained the meaning of arrogance (al-kibr), saying: «Arrogance is disdaining the truth and «غمس» people», that is, despising them. [Translator's note: the well-known wording of the ḥadīth is «وغمط الناس»; the text here reads «وغمس».] And in the ḥadīth of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar from the Prophet ﷺ: «The arrogant will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection like the forms of tiny ants; abasement will overtake them, until they are brought to a prison in Hell».

nahhas-irab:61-61.t:
وَيُنَجِّي اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا بِمَفازَتِهِمْ لا يَمَسُّهُمُ السُّوءُ وَلا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ (61) وَيُنَجِّي اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا بِمَفازَتِهِمْ: this is the reading of most people, in the singular, because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun).
The Kufans read «بمفازاتهم» (in the plural), and that is permissible, just as you say «بسعاداتهم» ("by their felicities"). The explanation of this verse is reported from the Prophet ﷺ in the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayra, who said: «Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will gather every man together with his deeds; the deeds of the believer will be with him in the finest form, and whenever there is terror or fear, they will say to him: "Do not be alarmed; you are not the one intended by it, nor are you the one meant by it." When that becomes much for him, he will say to it: "How beautiful you are! Who are you?"
It will say: "Do you not know me? I am your righteous deeds; you carried me despite my heaviness, so by Allah, I will carry you today and defend you." That is what He said: وَيُنَجِّي اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا بِمَفازَتِهِمْ لا يَمَسُّهُمُ السُّوءُ وَلا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ».

nahhas-irab:62-62.t: That is, He is its Preserver and the One who sustains it.

nahhas-irab:63-63.t: لَهُ مَقالِيدُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ: its singular is «مقليد», though what is mostly used for it is «إقليد». وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآياتِ اللَّهِ is a mubtadaʾ (subject); أُولئِكَ هُمُ: a second mubtadaʾ; الْخاسِرُونَ is the khabar (predicate) of the second, and «هم» is a separating pronoun (fāṣila). It is also possible that «أولئك» is a badal (substitute) for «الذين», with «هم» a mubtadaʾ and «الخاسرون» its khabar, the clause being the khabar of «الذين».

nahhas-irab:64-64.t:
«غير» is accusative by «أعبد». Al-Kisāʾī holds that the implied form is «أن أعبد», then «أن» was omitted and the verb became nominative; and this is one of Sībawayh's two views on this أَعْبُدُ. His other view is that the implied form is «أفغير الله أعبد فيما تأمروني» ("Is it other than Allah that I should worship, in what you command me?"), and this is a clear view; that is: "Is it other than Allah that I should worship — you command me [that]?", and in this there is the meaning of "in your command". Al-Akhfash Saʿīd says: «تأمروني» is suspended (mulghā), just as you say: «قال ذلك زيد بلغني» ("Zayd said that, it reached me"). And this is exactly Sībawayh's view. As for [the claim] that something governs the accusative and then, when it is omitted, its governing becomes stronger so that it governs the nominative, its error is evident. Had you made «أن» overt here it would not be permissible, and it would be a separation between the ṣila (relative clause) and the relative. The original is «تأمرونني»; the nūn was assimilated into the nūn. As for «تأمروني» with a single light nūn, the like of it occurs only anomalously in poetry, and Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, may Allah have mercy on him, says it is a solecism (laḥn). Sībawayh recited, regarding the like of it: [al-Wāfir] 392-
ترعاه كالثّغام يعلّ مسكا ... يسوء الفاليات إذا فليني
("[Hair] that she sees like the white thughām plant, drenched again and again with musk; it grieves the women who search it for lice when they search me.")
And I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: the grammarians of old used to marvel at the eloquence of Jarīr and his saying, extempore, «إنهم يبدؤوني» ("they begin with me"). As for the omission of the yāʾ from «تأمروني», that is easy, because the nūn is as it were a substitute for it and the kasra indicates it.

nahhas-irab:65-65.t:
وَلَقَدْ أُوحِيَ إِلَيْكَ وَإِلَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ لَئِنْ أَشْرَكْتَ لَيَحْبَطَنَّ عَمَلُكَ: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said:
[it means] "it will surely be corrupted"; and he held that it is from their saying «حبط بطنه يحبط» and «حبج يحبج», when [the belly] is corrupted by a particular disease.

nahhas-irab:66-66.t:
بَلِ اللَّهَ فَاعْبُدْ: Abū Jaʿfar said: in my book from Abū Isḥāq, the word «الله», the name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is accusative by «اعبد». He said: and there is no disagreement about this among the Basrans and the Kufans. Abū Jaʿfar said:
But al-Farrāʾ said: it is accusative by an implied verb, because it is a command. As for the fāʾ, Abū Isḥāq said: it is for the requital (mujāzāh), and others say that it is redundant (zāʾida). [Translator's note: the printed text reads «فأمال الفاء»; it appears to be a corruption of «فأمّا الفاء» ("as for the fāʾ"), and has been translated accordingly.]

nahhas-irab:67-67.t: وَما قَدَرُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: that is, [they did not] magnify Him, from your saying «فلان عظيم القدر» ("so-and-so is of great standing"). Abū Jaʿfar said: so the meaning on this basis is: and they did not magnify Allah with the magnification due to Him, since they worshipped others alongside Him, while He is the Creator of things and their Owner. وَالْأَرْضُ جَمِيعاً قَبْضَتُهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). Al-Farrāʾ permitted «قبضته» in the accusative, with the meaning "in His grasp". Abū Isḥāq said: it has not been read so, and it is an error according to the Basrans; it is not permissible: they do not say «زيد قبضتك» nor «المال قبضتك», meaning "in your grasp". He said: and if this were permissible, «زيد دارك», meaning "in your house", would be permissible. وَالسَّماواتُ مَطْوِيَّاتٌ بِيَمِينِهِ: a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. Al-Kisāʾī, al-Farrāʾ and Abū Isḥāq permitted «مطويّات» with kasra on the tāʾ [i.e. accusative]; Abū Isḥāq said: as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:68-70.t:
ثُمَّ نُفِخَ فِيهِ أُخْرى فَإِذا هُمْ قِيامٌ يَنْظُرُونَ: al-Kisāʾī permitted «قياما» in the accusative, just as you say:
«خرجت فإذا زيد جالسا» ("I went out, and there was Zayd, sitting"). Zayd ibn Aslam said regarding His saying, Mighty and Majestic: وَجِيءَ بِالنَّبِيِّينَ وَالشُّهَداءِ: the witnesses are the recording guardian angels (al-ḥafaẓa).

nahhas-irab:71-73.t:
وَسِيقَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِلى جَهَنَّمَ زُمَراً: [زُمَراً] is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). حَتَّى إِذا جاؤُها فُتِحَتْ أَبْوابُها: [فُتِحَتْ] is the answer of «إذا». And in the account of the people of Paradise: وَفُتِحَتْ, with the wāw. The Kufans say:
the wāw is redundant (zāʾida); and this is an error according to the Basrans, because it conveys a meaning, namely conjunction here, and the answer is omitted. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: that is, "they were made happy". The omission of the answer is eloquent in the speech of the Arabs, and he recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 393-
فلو أنّها نفس تموت سويّة ... ولكنّها نفس تساقط أنفسا
("If only it were a soul that died all at once — but it is a soul that falls away soul by soul.")
So he omitted the answer of «لو», the implied meaning being: "it would have been more restful". As for the wisdom in keeping the wāw in the second and omitting it from the first, one of the people of knowledge spoke about it — he says: I do not know that anyone preceded him to it — and it is that he said: when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said about the people of the Fire حَتَّى إِذا جاؤُها وَفُتِحَتْ أَبْوابُها, He indicated by this that it had been closed; and when He said about the people of Paradise حَتَّى إِذا جاؤُها وَفُتِحَتْ أَبْوابُها, He indicated by this that it had been open before they came to it. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows best. [Translator's note: in the verse about the people of the Fire (39:71) the Qurʾānic text is «فُتِحَتْ أَبْوابُها» without the wāw; the text here quotes it with the wāw, apparently a slip in the source, since the argument depends on the wāw being absent there.]

nahhas-irab:74-74.t: وَأَوْرَثَنَا الْأَرْضَ نَتَبَوَّأُ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ حَيْثُ نَشاءُ: we have already mentioned the view of Qatāda that it is the land of Paradise; and it has been said: it is the land of this world, on the basis of advancing and postponing [in the word order] (al-taqdīm wa-l-taʾkhīr).

nahhas-irab:75-75.t: حَافِّينَ: al-Akhfash said: its singular is «حافّ»; and al-Farrāʾ said: no singular is used for them, because this noun applies to them only when they are together. وَقِيلَ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ: that is, the believers say: praise be to Allah who rewarded us — to Him belongs the praise for the blessings and kindness with which He rewarded us, and for helping us against those who wronged us.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: تَنْزِيلُ الْكِتابِ is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is مِنَ اللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَكِيمِ, that is, sent down from Allah, Majestic and Mighty. It may also be nominative in the sense of "this is the sending down of the Book". Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ permitted تَنْزِيلَ الْكِتابِ «[Translator's note: the source prints the nominative vowelling.]» in the accusative, as an object. Al-Kisāʾī said: that is, follow and recite the sending down of the Book. Al-Farrāʾ said: by way of incitement (ighrāʾ), like كِتابَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ [al-Nisāʾ: 24], that is, hold fast to the Book of Allah.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: أَلا لِلَّهِ الدِّينُ الْخالِصُ: that is, that which nothing adulterates. In the ḥadīth of al-Ḥasan from Abū Hurayra, a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, I give something in charity and do something intending by it the Face of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and the praise of people." The Prophet ﷺ said: «By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muḥammad, Allah, exalted be His praise, does not accept anything in which [another] is made a partner. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: أَلا لِلَّهِ الدِّينُ الْخالِصُ» ] «[Translator's note: a stray bracket stands here in the source.]». وَالَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِهِ أَوْلِياءَ is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the implied form is: and those who have taken protectors besides Him said: ما نَعْبُدُهُمْ إِلَّا لِيُقَرِّبُونا إِلَى اللَّهِ زُلْفى. It is also possible that «الذين» is in the position of the nominative by their verb, that is, and [they] said «[Translator's note: the sentence appears incomplete in the source.]». «زلفى» is in the position of the accusative in the sense of a maṣdar (verbal noun), that is, a bringing near.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: لَوْ أَرادَ اللَّهُ أَنْ يَتَّخِذَ وَلَداً لَاصْطَفى مِمَّا يَخْلُقُ ما يَشاءُ: that is, if He had wanted that — to name anyone of His creation with this — He would not have left it to them. سُبْحانَهُ is a maṣdar (verbal noun), that is, a declaring of Him far above having a child.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: that is, He lays this over that and that over this. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is the meaning of التكوير (wrapping) in the language. Something other than this has been reported from Ibn ʿAbbās on the meaning of the verse; he said: what is lessened from the night enters into the day, and what is lessened from the day enters into the night.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: That is, darkness does not hinder Him as it hinders created beings.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: وَإِنْ تَشْكُرُوا يَرْضَهُ لَكُمْ: that is, He approves gratitude for you; [the verb] تشكروا indicates the gratitude.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: دَعا رَبَّهُ مُنِيباً: [منيبا] as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:9-9.t:
أَمَّنْ هُوَ قانِتٌ is the reading of al-Ḥasan, Abū ʿAmr, Abū Jaʿfar, ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī. Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read أَمَّنْ هُوَ «[Translator's note: i.e. the light form أَمَنْ; the source prints the doubled form.]». Abū Ḥātim reported from al-Akhfash, who said: whoever reads أَمَّنْ هُوَ in al-Zumar with the light form, his reading is weak, because it is a question with no predicate accompanying it. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is not binding; they all agreed on reading «أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام», and that is like it. In the reading with the light form there are two good explanations in Arabic, whereas in the other reading there is only one explanation. One of the two explanations is that it is a vocative, as one says يا زيد أقبل (O Zayd, come), and one says أزيد أقبل; Sībawayh and all the grammarians reported that, as [the poet] said: [al-Kāmil] 386-
أبني لبينى لستم بيد ... إلّا يدا ليست لها عضد
(O sons of Lubaynā, you are not a hand — unless a hand that has no upper arm.)
And as one says: so-and-so does not pray or fast — O you who pray and fast, rejoice! The other explanation is that it is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the meaning is known, that is: is one who is devoutly obedient in the hours of the night better, or one who sets up rivals to Allah? The implied form is: the one who is devoutly obedient. Whoever reads أَمَّنْ هُوَ, its implied form is: or rather is the one who is devoutly obedient better than the one mentioned; and «أم» means «أبل» (or rather, …?). As for the meaning of قانت: according to what ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith transmitted from Darrāj, from Abū al-Haytham, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: «Every qunūt in the Qurʾān is obedience to Allah, Majestic and Mighty». Al-Aʿmash transmitted from Abū Sufyān, from Jābir, that he said:
«The Prophet ﷺ was asked which prayer is best. He said: long qunūt»; a group of scholars interpreted it to mean long standing. ʿAbd Allāh transmitted from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, that he was asked about qunūt and said: I do not know qunūt except as long standing and reciting the Qurʾān. Mujāhid said: part of qunūt is long bowing and lowering the gaze. When the scholars stood in prayer they lowered their gaze and were humble, did not turn around in their prayer, did not fidget, and did not mention anything of worldly affairs except forgetfully. Abū Jaʿfar said:
The root of this is that qunūt is obedience, and everything said about it is obedience to Allah, Majestic and Mighty; all these things are included in obedience, and more than them — as Nāfiʿ said: Ibn ʿUmar said to me: "Get up and pray." So I got up to pray, and I had on a worn-out garment. He called me and said to me: "Do you think, if I sent you on an errand behind the wall, would you go like this?" I said: "No, I would adorn myself." He said: "Then Allah is more deserving that one adorn oneself for Him."
Al-Ḥasan said: آناءَ اللَّيْلِ are its hours: its beginning, its middle and its end.
From Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: آناءَ اللَّيْلِ is the depth of the night. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: يَحْذَرُ الْآخِرَةَ, that is, the punishment of the Hereafter. قُلْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِي الَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُونَ وَالَّذِينَ لا يَعْلَمُونَ: Abū Isḥāq said: that is, just as those who know and those who do not know are not equal, so the obedient and the disobedient are not equal. Others said: those who know are those who benefit from their knowledge and act upon it; as for one who does not benefit from his knowledge and does not act on it, he is in the position of one who does not know. إِنَّما يَتَذَكَّرُ أُولُوا الْأَلْبابِ: that is, only those of intelligence, who benefit from their intellects, benefit from His reminder, profit by it and take heed; so these benefit and are praised for their intellects, because they benefited from them.

nahhas-irab:10-13.t:
قُلْ يا عِبادِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمْ: it has been said that its meaning is: beware of disobeying Him. The tāʾ [in اتّقوا] is a substitute for a wāw.
لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا فِي هذِهِ الدُّنْيا حَسَنَةٌ: "in this world" may be included in the ṣila (relative clause), that is, they will have good in the Hereafter; and if it is not included in the ṣila, the meaning is: for those who do good there is good in this world.
The good that they have in this world is Allah's befriending them, Majestic and Mighty, His praise of them and His calling them by fine names. وَأَرْضُ اللَّهِ واسِعَةٌ: there are two views on its meaning. One is that by it is meant the land of the Garden. The other is that its meaning is: Allah's earth is wide, so emigrate in it and do not stay with those who commit sins.
إِنَّما يُوَفَّى الصَّابِرُونَ أَجْرَهُمْ: صابر, used in praise, refers only to one who is patient in refraining from sins; if you mean that he persists in sin, you say صابر على كذا. بِغَيْرِ حِسابٍ: it has been said: without measure; and it has been said: what is meant is over and above the reward, because if he were given in proportion to what he did, it would be by reckoning. It has also been said that the meaning of «بغير حساب» is: without pursuit or demand [for account], as demand [for account] occurs regarding the blessings of this world.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: قُلِ اللَّهَ أَعْبُدُ: accusative by أعبد. Sībawayh permits the nominative with the hāʾ omitted [i.e. as if اللهُ أعبده], but we know of no grammarian who agreed with him on that in the case of a proper name.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: الَّذِينَ is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إِنَّ. أَهْلِيهِمْ is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to أنفسهم, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ. Maymūn ibn Mihrān said, from Ibn ʿAbbās: there is no one but Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has created for him a wife in the Garden; so when he enters the Fire he has lost himself and his family.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t:
لَهُمْ مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ ظُلَلٌ مِنَ النَّارِ: the singular is ظلّة, which is whatever of the Fire rises above them and stays fixed.
وَمِنْ تَحْتِهِمْ ظُلَلٌ is figurative, that is, the like of that beneath them. It has also been said: it is literal, that is, beneath them are canopies for those of the people of the Fire who are lower than them. ذلِكَ is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), that is, that punishment which We have mentioned is that with which Allah frightens His servants. يا عِبادِ فَاتَّقُونِ: with the yāʾ of عبادي dropped, because the vocative is a place of omission; it is permissible to retain it according to the original, and it is permissible to give it a fatḥa.

nahhas-irab:17-19.t: وَالَّذِينَ اجْتَنَبُوا الطَّاغُوتَ أَنْ يَعْبُدُوها: al-Akhfash said: الطاغوت is a plural, and it may be a feminine singular.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: وَعْدَ اللَّهِ is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of لَهُمْ غُرَفٌ is: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has promised them that as a promise. The nominative is permissible, in the sense of "that is the promise of Allah".

nahhas-irab:21-21.t:
فَسَلَكَهُ يَنابِيعَ فِي الْأَرْضِ: its singular is ينبوع; one also says ينبع, and its plural is ينابيع. One says نبع الماء ينبُع and ينبِع. Ibn Kaysān reported to us concerning the poet's saying: [al-Kāmil] 387-
ينباع من ذفرى غضوب جسرة
(It oozes from behind the ear of an irritable, bold she-camel.)
that its meaning is ينبع, and he lengthened the fatḥa so that it became an alif. ثُمَّ يَهِيجُ: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: al-Aṣmaʿī said: one says هاجت الأرض تهيج when its vegetation passes and withers. He said: and others than al-Aṣmaʿī said the same. ثُمَّ يَجْعَلُهُ حُطاماً: he said: from the breaking of a stalk when it crumbles from dryness. إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَذِكْرى لِأُولِي الْأَلْبابِ: its singular is ذو, and it is a collective noun; according to some of the people of language, a wāw was added in its spelling to distinguish it from إلى.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: أَفَمَنْ شَرَحَ اللَّهُ صَدْرَهُ لِلْإِسْلامِ: Abū Isḥāq said: this fāʾ is the fāʾ of requital (al-mujāzāh). فَوَيْلٌ لِلْقاسِيَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: one says قسا when something becomes hard. He said: and likewise عتا and عسا, which are close to it. قلب قاس is a hard heart that does not become tender or soft. أُولئِكَ is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), that is, those whose hearts have hardened are فِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t:
اللَّهُ نَزَّلَ أَحْسَنَ الْحَدِيثِ كِتاباً مُتَشابِهاً: [كتابا] is a badal (substitute) for أحسن. مَثانِيَ is a naʿt (adjective) of كتاب.
It is a diptote because it is a plural with no counterpart among singulars. تَقْشَعِرُّ مِنْهُ is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of كتاب. ذلِكَ is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), that is, that fear, hope and softening of hearts is هُدَى اللَّهِ.

nahhas-irab:24-25.t: أَفَمَنْ يَتَّقِي بِوَجْهِهِ سُوءَ الْعَذابِ: the apodosis is omitted. Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: that is, is one who shields himself with his face from the evil punishment better, or one who is happy [in the Garden]?

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: فَأَذاقَهُمُ اللَّهُ: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: of anything that reaches a bodily organ one says "it has tasted it", that is, it has reached it, as sweetness and bitterness reach the one who tastes them. He said: الخزي is what is hateful, and الخزاء is excessive shame.

nahhas-irab:27-28.t: قُرْآناً عَرَبِيًّا is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Al-Akhfash said: because His saying, Majestic and Mighty, في هذا القرآن is definite. ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: «عربيا» is accusative as a ḥāl, and قرآنا is a preparatory ḥāl (tawṭiʾat al-ḥāl), as you say: مررت بزيد رجلا صالحا, where your word صالحا is what is accusative as a ḥāl. Abū Isḥāq said: «قرآنا عربيا» is a ḥāl; and he said: «قرآنا» is for emphasis (tawkīd). غَيْرَ ذِي عِوَجٍ is a naʿt (adjective). The best that has been said about it is what al-Ḍaḥḥāk said; he said: [not] inconsistent.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t:
ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا رَجُلًا فِيهِ شُرَكاءُ مُتَشاكِسُونَ: al-Farrāʾ said: that is, at variance. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: that is, quarrelsome with one another, from شكس يشكس, so he is شكس, like عسر يعسر عسرا, so he is عسر.
وَرَجُلًا سَلَماً لِرَجُلٍ: this is the reading of the people of Medina and the people of Kufa. Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, al-Jaḥdarī, Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr read وَرَجُلًا سَلَماً «[Translator's note: i.e. سالِماً; the source prints سَلَماً for both readings.]», and Ibn ʿAbbās explained it, saying:
Belonging wholly [to one]. Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū ʿUbayd inclined to this reading, saying: because سالم is the opposite of "shared", while سلم is the opposite of war, and "one at war" has no meaning here. Abū Jaʿfar said: this argument is not binding, because when a word has two meanings it is construed only according to the more fitting of the two; and this, even if سلم is the opposite of war, has another use, as one says: you had partners in this house, and it has become سلم to you (wholly yours). And the same objection binds him regarding سالم as what he raised against the other, because one says شيء سالم, something free of any defect. Both readings are good; the leading readers have read with both.

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: The reading of Ibn Muḥayṣin, Ibn Abī Isḥāq and ʿĪsā is إنّك مائت وإنّهم مائتون. Abū Jaʿfar said: it is a good reading, and an alif like this is dropped in the script. مائت for the future is common in the speech of the Arabs; similar to it: ما كان مريضا وإنّه لمارض من هذا الطعام (he was not ill, but he will become ill from this food). ميّت is also permissible, and its lightened form [ميْت] is permissible according to all except Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, for he did not permit the lightened form for the future.

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: It has been said: meaning concerning wrongs [done to one another]. In the ḥadīth with a connected chain: «The first thing in which disputes will occur is blood».

nahhas-irab:32-32.t:
أَلَيْسَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ مَثْوىً لِلْكافِرِينَ: مَثْوىً is in the position of the nominative, and its inflection is not visible because it ends in an alif maqṣūra. It is derived from ثوى يثوي; had it been from أثوى, it would be مُثْوى «[Translator's note: the source does not vowel the form; the sense requires مُثْوًى.]». This indicates that ثوى is the eloquent dialectal form. Abū ʿUbayda reported أثوى, and recited: [al-Kāmil] 388-
أثوى وقصّر ليلة ليزوّدا
(He stayed, and cut short a night, to be given provisions.)
Al-Aṣmaʿī knows only ثوى, and transmits it as أثوى «[Translator's note: so in the source; presumably he transmits the verse with ثوى, e.g. أَثَوى as a question.]».

nahhas-irab:33-35.t: وَالَّذِي جاءَ بِالصِّدْقِ is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is أُولئِكَ هُمُ الْمُتَّقُونَ. Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī interpreted it as referring to a group, and said: الَّذِي جاءَ بِالصِّدْقِ are the believers who will come with the Qurʾān on the Day of Resurrection and say: this is what you gave us; we have followed what is in it. On this view الذي has a plural sense, as «من» has a plural sense. It has also been said: rather, the nūn [of الذين] was dropped because of the length of the noun. Al-Shaʿbī interpreted it as singular, and said: the one who came with the truth is Muḥammad ﷺ, and the one who confirmed it is Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah be pleased with him, and the Companions; on this view its khabar is plural, as one says of someone who is honoured: "they did such and such". Another answer is that it refers to him ﷺ and to those who followed him. In the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: والذين جاءوا بالصدق وصدّقوا به; this is a reading by way of exegesis. In the reading of Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Kūfī: وَالَّذِي جاءَ بِالصِّدْقِ وَصَدَقَ بِهِ «[Translator's note: the source prints the standard صَدَّقَ.]» with the light form; its meaning — and Allah knows best — would be "and was truthful in it", as one says فلان بمكّة and في مكّة (so-and-so is at Mecca / in Mecca).

nahhas-irab:36-37.t: أَلَيْسَ اللَّهُ بِكافٍ عَبْدَهُ: the yāʾ was dropped because it is unvowelled and the nunation after it is unvowelled. The original would be for it not to be dropped in pause, since the nunation disappears; but it was dropped so that it may be known that it is so in continuous speech. Some Arabs retain it in pause according to the original, saying: كافي عبده.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t:
هَلْ هُنَّ كاشِفاتُ ضُرِّهِ without nunation is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar, Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī. Abū ʿAmr and Shayba read — and it is the well-known reading of al-Ḥasan and ʿĀṣim — هَلْ هُنَّ كاشِفاتُ ضُرِّهِ and مُمْسِكاتُ رَحْمَتِهِ with nunation «[Translator's note: i.e. كاشِفاتٌ ضُرَّهُ and مُمْسِكاتٌ رَحْمَتَهُ; the source prints the forms without nunation.]», according to the original, because it has not yet happened; were it past, nunation would not be permissible in it. Dropping the nunation is for lightness; when the nunation is dropped, no barrier remains between the two nouns, so you put the second in the genitive by the iḍāfa. Dropping the nunation is frequent in the speech of the Arabs, current and good. Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: هَدْياً بالِغَ الْكَعْبَةِ [al-Māʾida:
95], and likewise هذا عارِضٌ مُمْطِرُنا [al-Aḥqāf: 24], and likewise إِنَّا مُرْسِلُوا النَّاقَةِ [al-Qamar: 27].
Sībawayh said: the like of that is frequent; similar to it is غَيْرَ مُحِلِّي الصَّيْدِ [al-Māʾida: 1], because its meaning is like the meaning of وَلَا آمِّينَ الْبَيْتَ الْحَرامَ [al-Māʾida: 2]. Sībawayh recited: [al-Basīṭ]
389-
هل أنت باعث دينار لحاجتنا ... أو عبد ربّ أخا عون بن مخراق
(Will you send Dīnār for our need, or ʿAbd Rabb, the brother of ʿAwn ibn Mikhrāq?)
And al-Nābigha said: [al-Basīṭ] 390-
واحكم كحكم فتاة الحيّ إذ نظرت ... إلى حمام شراع وارد الثمد
(Judge like the judgement of the tribe's maiden when she looked at a flock of doves heading to the shallow pool.)
Its meaning is وارد الثّمد «[Translator's note: i.e. واردٍ الثمدَ with nunation; the source does not vowel it.]», and he dropped the nunation, like «كاشفات ضرّه».

nahhas-irab:39-40.t: قُلْ يا قَوْمِ اعْمَلُوا عَلى مَكانَتِكُمْ إِنِّي عامِلٌ: on my مكانة, that is, on my course which has become established with me.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: It has been said: its meaning is: that you may make it clear to people with the truth that they were commanded concerning it.

nahhas-irab:42-43.t:
فَيُمْسِكُ الَّتِي قَضى عَلَيْهَا الْمَوْتَ: the reading of Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī is فَيُمْسِكُ الَّتِي قَضى عَلَيْهَا الْمَوْتَ ] «[Translator's note: i.e. قُضِيَ عَلَيْهَا الْمَوْتُ; the source prints the standard vowelling, followed by a stray bracket.]» as [a verb] whose agent is not named (passive). The meaning is the same, except that the first reading is clearer and more consistent with the arrangement of the speech, because they agreed on «ويرسل» and did not read ويُرسَل [in the passive]. The reason for the fatḥa of the wāw in His saying, Majestic and Mighty:
أَوَلَوْ كانُوا لا يَمْلِكُونَ شَيْئاً وَلا يَعْقِلُونَ has already been given in the book before this.

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: [جميعا] is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). If it is said: جميع applies only to two or more, while intercession is one — the answer is that الشفاعة is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and a maṣdar stands for two and for a plural.

nahhas-irab:45-45.t: وَإِذا ذُكِرَ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ: [وحده] is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, and as a ḥāl (circumstantial) according to Yūnus. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: اشْمَأَزَّتْ, that is, shrank [in aversion].

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: قُلِ اللَّهُمَّ فاطِرَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ: accusative because it is a vocative in construct; likewise عالِمَ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهادَةِ. According to Sībawayh it is not permissible for it to be a naʿt (adjective) [of اللهمّ].
